compiled_kernel_resources.scope: Static compiler declarations, not measured occupancy.

implementation: An isolated copy of the original C64 producer stores center/error checkpoints at one half or three quarters. Final centers, errors and candidate sets remain bit-identical to original C64. Each original exact K16 segment carries its full significand/exponent/sign into the next segment. The coarse error increment final.error-prefix.error bounds the suffix sum of native, canonical and center-addition errors along the same original path. Therefore exact_prefix+final.center-prefix.center is a new center; outward bounds also cover its two FP32 arithmetic operations. A common BF16 endpoint permits early completion. Other outputs compact their original exact carry in a 12-byte record and continue the next disjoint K segment. Unsupported intervals continue all original groups. Compaction is between kernels so later groups are not left in inactive SIMD subgroups. The native zero-C coefficient remains the existing conditional2^-19 assumption; finite tests do not prove a universal hardware bound.
correctness_scope: Independent wide CPU arithmetic checks generated canonical groups under three modeled native errors and every suffix interval. Native generated fixtures include row/token tails, zeros, cancellation, unsupported operands and widths through8192. Complete candidate membership, compacted continuation/completion partitions, explicit state fields, unused workspace tails and guards are checked. Every generated continuation carry and sampled captured carries agree with independent CPU prefixes; snapshot and suffix intervals are checked against independent CPU prefixes. All final captured outputs agree with GB10 BF16 references on the warmup, every measured attempt and separate audit runs. Full-replay endpoints preserve original raw FP32 values; early-certified endpoints promise the same BF16 value, not identical raw FP32. Reference tensors and canonical outputs are comparison data only. The original7169 inputs plus first1023 repeated rows form the q8192 operator shape; this is not new model inference. Fixture CPU counts repeat in each variant report and are deduplicated in verified_counts.
timing_scope: Four variants: original C64 plus full replay, four-part snapshot storage plus full replay, two-part phased replay, four-part phased replay. One warmup plus three completed host samples rotate whole-operator variant order. Timers include lossless preparation, eligibility, the entire matrix producer, initial selection and host count read, every exact segment, continuation compaction, state transfers and additional count reads. Allocation, initial buffer clearing, reference computation, validation and separate audits are outside timers. All buffers are preallocated; both continuation arrays and the maximum three-snapshot allocation exist in all arms. Thus this is not the allocation-owning production owner or a TTFT measurement. QKV controls use C64 and do not replace the faster retained QKV matrix route.

decision.reason: Four stages remove31.6731% of selected OUT K16 groups and save13.2318 ms including the new pipeline. QKV removes27.6080% of selected groups but the four-part route is13.9187 ms slower than its C64 control; checkpoint storage alone costs38.3414 ms. The two-part QKV difference is only-2.4642 ms against a C64 baseline that is not the retained QKV producer. This is useful exact-work reduction evidence, but no seconds-scale model gain is established. Keep current product dispatch while pursuing broader producer or replay replacements.
